name: Belonger Status by Descent

qualifying_event.description: Belonger status attaches by descent under Section 2(2) of the Immigration Act to: (a) a person born in Montserrat before 1 January 1983, or registered/naturalised as a citizen of the United Kingdom and Colonies before that date; (b) a person born in Montserrat on or after 1 January 1983 to a parent who was a British Dependent Territories Citizen or 'settled' in Montserrat at the time; (c) a person whose parent or grandparent was born, registered, or naturalised in Montserrat under the British Nationality Act 1948, or who was born outside Montserrat after 1983 to a parent born, registered, or naturalised there; and (d) certain Commonwealth citizens with a grandparent born or naturalised in Montserrat, and children under 18 of a Belonger.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Birth certificates (applicant, parent, grandparent as relevant); citizenship/registration/naturalisation documents; proof of parent's 'settled' status where applicable.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires meeting one of the descent/birth grounds in Section 2(2) of the Immigration Act: birth in Montserrat before 1983 (or naturalisation/registration before then), birth after 1983 to a settled/BDTC parent, descent from a parent or grandparent born/naturalised in Montserrat, or (for certain Commonwealth citizens) a grandparent born/naturalised in Montserrat.

evidence_required.document: Parent's and/or grandparent's birth, registration, or naturalisation documents
Proof of parent's British Dependent Territories citizenship or 'settled' status, where the applicant was born after 1983

sources.title: Montserrat Chapter 13.01, Immigration Act -- Section 2(2), definition of 'belonger' by birth, descent, and registration/naturalisation

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of Montserrat's initial build; Montserrat is the second British Overseas Territory (BOT) built this session, after Anguilla. Same key modelling decision as Anguilla applies and is only explained once here for Montserrat: Belonger status is Montserrat's own local legal status (a right-of-abode-equivalent), not British nationality -- formal British Overseas Territories Citizenship (BOTC) is a separate track (see ms_naturalisation.json), so leads_to_citizenship is modelled as false here even though descent-based routes lead directly to citizenship in every non-BOT country built this session. Unlike Anguilla, Montserrat's Immigration Act does not appear to include a long-term-residence-only ground for Belonger status (no equivalent of Anguilla's 15-year residence path was found in Section 2(2)) -- so no ms_belonger_status_residence.json file was created; this is a genuine legal difference between the two territories' Belonger regimes, not an oversight, and is flagged here in case a residence-based ground exists elsewhere in the Act and was missed in this pass. Section 2(2)'s birth-before-1983 and birth-after-1983-to-settled-parent grounds are automatic-by-birth provisions rather than something a person migrates to qualify for -- they are included in this route's qualifying_event description for completeness of the legal definition, but the requirement_groups model the descent/lineage grounds most relevant to an immigration dataset (a person establishing Belonger status via ancestry rather than their own birth in Montserrat).
